correctness.rationale: One claim is proved for each n≥2 and strictly positive w. Sorting-chamber linearity and the quotient first-difference ℓ1 norm give exact maximum rank-constrained cut formula and attainability by two data vectors. For sine weights, the largest allowable number of binary boundary crossings and unimodality give a sharp central cut whose trigonometric sum equals K_n s_j. The canonical feasible cut matrix A satisfies As=K_ns, yielding a universal minimax lower bound by a smallest-coordinate argument. Its central row covers all edges, enforcing optimizer uniqueness. Exact rational cut tests and actual chamber extremizer checks independently exercise critical finite formulas; infinite-size generality comes from the argument.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Classical Hardy–Littlewood–Pólya majorization and Pólya–Szegő yield rearrangement contraction of one input, and sorting is contractive in ordinary symmetric coordinate norms. These stronger-looking norm classes do not include arbitrarily positioned weighted path-edge difference seminorms of two outputs. The full path two-input result does not follow from the inspected statements.

value.rationale: Classical sorting decreases variation of an individual signal but may strongly amplify variation of a perturbation. The result supplies an exact finite weighted two-input stability invariant and solves the natural all-positive-weights minimax design with a unique sine metric and explicit even/odd sharp constants. It reduces asymptotic worst-case sensitivity from n to (2/π)n, exposing a nonlinear permutation-chamber instability mechanism applicable to variation-aware ranking/rearrangement.
